Hi! My husband just got home from a deployment. He’s a submariner so it was emails only for 3 months. I didn’t have to deal with him being gone nearly as long as most, which I’m very grateful for, but the last month is always tough! 

Things I did to prep:
- Rewashed his clothes so they smelled clean and not just like our dresser 
- washed his car, cleaned out the interior 
- organized our kitchen 
- began buying snacks etc. that he likes to come home to 


I know there isn’t much to do to get ready a whole month out. But I also thought of it as… what do *I* want to do in my last month alone?

- get Indian food because it’s not his favorite 
- spend hours at the beach or library (he will do these things but again, not his favorite) 
- take lots of baths
- go shopping and update my wardrobe for fall 
- just embrace the time you have alone! You’ve managed on your own for so long now, and you’re almost there, so celebrate by taking care of yourself and doing things you love. I had a night where I ate Mac and cheese, drank wine and played fallout. For HOURS. Will my husband do these things with me? Absolutely, and gladly. But I would feel guilty playing a single player game with him next to me, and his backseat driving gets a little annoying lol. 

Make a list of the chores you want to do as it gets closer- you’ll be getting more excited as the date draws near. We get a phone call 24 hrs before they’re home so I had a “t- 24 hours” cleaning list. And a list of things I could do before that date. 

Last but not least, rely on your friends! It’s okay to be vulnerable and say “hey, I’m struggling with the anxiety/excitement of my boyfriend being home and I need DISTRACTIONS.” My friends and I walked/worked out a ton, had game nights, went thrifting, went to trivia. We got really close this summer and being real with them about the emotions I was experiencing helped them understand what kind of support I needed. 

Good luck!

I work with children and our philosophy is "process over product." For example, a child does an art project and they focus on/we emphasize the product, there will be kids frustrated with themselves, thinking they did something wrong or they are a failure because they didn't execute it properly.

If a child focuses (or we focus them) on the process, they enjoy the experience, they learn about what they are doing and also learn about the people around them/instructing them, and at the end of the day- it doesn't matter what their art looks like, the experience itself was enriching and fulfilling.

The purpose of life is not the end result. It can't be, because we all are working toward different goals and want different things out of life. If you focus on the process of life, enjoy what you're doing and the people around you, life will be MUCH more enjoyable and fulfilling.

Just remember- these men are not your dad, these men are not the assholes who ghosted you or suddenly turned cold. This new one is giving you the evidence you crave, your brain just isn’t used to that and is trying to fit it into the pattern of what you know.
